newsitem.title: GABON: Mobutu delays departure to meet Mbeki in Gabon.
newsitem.headline: Mobutu delays departure to meet Mbeki in Gabon.

text.p: Zaire's embattled President Mobutu Sese Seko delayed his return to his capital Kinshasa on Friday for talks in Gabon with South Africa's vice-president Thabo Mbeki, a Zairean foreign ministry official said.
Mbeki was expected in Gabon's capital Libreville later in the day from Zaire's second city of Lubumbashi, which he visited for talks with rebel leader Laurent Kabila, the official added.
"We are waiting for the vice-president of South Africa to arrive," the official told Reuters, adding that Mobutu would return to Kinshasa on Saturday -- one day later than planned.
Mbeki is trying to build on talks between Mobutu and Kabila hosted by South Africa's president, Nelson Mandela, on a South African ship on Sunday.
Senior U.N. sources in Geneva said the two civil war rivals had agreed to meet on the ship again on Wednesday.

Mobutu and a handful of fellow French-speaking Central African presidents held a summit in Gabon on Thursday. The Central African leaders welcomed a decision by Mobutu not to seek reelection, saying it opened a way for a peaceful end to the war and gave its transitional parliament a key role.

Mobutu and the presidents of Gabon, Chad, Congo, Central African Republic and Equatorial Guinea urged the parliament to fill the vacant post of speaker -- Mobutu's constitutional successor in the event of death or incapacity.
Officials in Kinshasa had said that Mobutu, who is fighting cancer and Kabila's rebels, would return home on Friday.
